title: Ploughman's Lunch
description: A traditional British cold plate with cheddar, bread, ham, apple, pickles, chutney, and crisp salad elements.
instructions: Arrange the bread, cheddar, ham, apple, pickles, chutney, and salad before serving so the cold plate feels balanced rather than randomly assembled.
Bring the cheddar slightly toward room temperature while keeping the meat chilled, because cheese tastes fuller when it is not fridge-cold.
Slice the bread thickly and butter it if desired, keeping the pieces rustic enough to hold cheese, ham, and chutney without falling apart.
Cut the apple at the last moment so it stays bright, then place it near the pickles and chutney to balance sharp, sweet, and savory flavors.
Fold or fan the ham neatly on the board, leaving space between wet pickles and bread so the bread does not become damp before eating.
Add salad leaves as a fresh element rather than a bulky garnish, then grind black pepper lightly over the cheese and apple.
Check that every serving has bread, cheese, ham, fruit, pickle, and chutney, which is the point of the classic ploughman's lunch.
Serve immediately at cool room temperature with a knife for the cheese and chutney, keeping any spare meat refrigerated until needed.
tips: Use room-temperature cheddar.
Slice apple just before serving.
Balance rich cheese with sharp pickles.
commonMistakes: Cold cheese tastes muted.
Too little chutney makes the plate dry.
Cutting bread too thin removes the rustic feel.
substitutions: Use Stilton for part of the cheddar.
Use pork pie instead of ham if desired.
Use Branston-style pickle for chutney.
storage: Assemble just before serving.
Refrigerate components separately for 2 days.
Do not store sliced apple without lemon.
